PROGRESS.md is gitignored (a task-tracking artifact, not repo content), so no additional commit is needed for it.

## Summary

Resolved PR #80's merge conflict against `origin/master`:

- The only real conflict was in `ai-os/OWNER_DIRECTIVES/PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml` — both PR #80 and master had independently appended a new `articles[]` entry with the same id `A15` off the same `A14` ancestor. Kept both articles' full content unchanged: PR #80's `A15_interactive_session_write_gate` as-is (it's cited by exact id elsewhere in `MASTER_INDEX.yaml`), and renumbered master's `A15_hold_for_owner_signoff` → `A16_hold_for_owner_signoff` to avoid a duplicate id (no other references to that id existed to break).
- `MASTER_INDEX.yaml` and everything else auto-merged cleanly with no conflict markers.
- Didn't touch the write-gate logic itself (guard snippet, `_lib.sh`, wrappers) — conflict resolution only, per constraints.
- Verified: `PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml` parses as valid YAML with 16 unique article ids; `tests/interactive_session_guard_test.sh` (the real write-gate suite) passes all 44 scenarios; full `pytest tests/` passes 36/36; two other guard-adjacent shell suites pass too.
- Note: `CONTROLLER.yaml` has a pre-existing YAML parse error (bad embedded quoting in a log entry around line 3517) present identically on both `origin/master` and PR #80's pre-merge tip — not caused by this merge, left untouched as out of scope.
- Committed (`481e4f0`) and pushed to PR #80's existing branch. `gh pr view 80` now reports `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`. PR was not merged, per constraints.
